title: Working Scientifically
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Working Scientifically Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_code: AC9S6I01, AC9S6I02, AC9S6I03, AC9S6I04, AC9S6I05, AC9S6I06
standard_text: Pose investigable questions and hypotheses; plan fair tests, identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables; use equipment and digital tools to collect data; construct and read tables and graphs; identify patterns and anomalies; evaluate methods; and communicate findings (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Year 6 science inquiry content descriptions).
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on working scientifically: hypotheses, independent, dependent and controlled variables, line and column graphs, anomalies, conclusions and evaluating evidence. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Change one, measure one, control the rest.
key_sub: The independent variable is changed, the dependent is measured, controlled variables stay the same.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every fair test has three kinds of variable.

  • Independent variable: the one you change on purpose (it goes on the bottom axis of a graph).
  • Dependent variable: the one you measure (it goes on the side axis).
  • Controlled variables: everything you keep the same. Repeat the test, look for the pattern, and check any result that does not fit.
Example

Ramp height and distance rolled. Which variable do you change?

you choose the ramp height

Answer: ramp height (independent)

Example

Temperature every 10 minutes. Which graph?

both variables are numbers

the data change over time

Answer: a line graph

Common mistakes

  • Swapping the independent variable (changed) and the dependent variable (measured).
  • Choosing a column graph for data that change over time.
  • Writing a conclusion that goes further than the results.

faq.q: What are independent, dependent and controlled variables?
faq.a: The independent variable is the one you change. The dependent variable is the one you measure. Controlled variables are kept the same so the test is fair.

faq.q: What is the difference between an observation and an inference?
faq.a: An observation is what you see or measure, such as 'the water reached 40 °C'. An inference is an explanation of it, such as 'dark colours absorb more light'.

faq.q: How do I read a line graph?
faq.a: Find the value on the bottom axis, go straight up to the line, then go across to the side axis and read the value. Check the units.
